label: Reply
description: Answer the caller of this run with one message. Behind a Route it is the response: status, headers and body, and the exchange ends. Behind a Socket it is one message and the socket stays open (status and headers have no meaning there and are refused if set). The body's shape follows the trigger's dataType: any value for json, a String for text, a stored file for bytes. On a json route a stored file anywhere in the body (a picture kept at project scope, say) goes out as `{ url, mimeType, filename, sizeBytes }`, the url being a link the caller can fetch straight into an ``.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: What to send: any value on a json route (an object, a list, a string), a String on a text route, a stored file on a bytes route.

inputs.name: status
inputs.label: Status
inputs.description: The HTTP status of the response (Route only).

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Extra response headers by name (Route only). A content-type here overrides the one the body's shape implies.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires true once the message has been handed to the caller.

then.message: Reply '{id}' answers nobody: no Route or Socket starts a run that reaches it. Wire it from the trigger's run (through data, or `_should_flow`), or put it in a group the trigger's `_should_flow` runs.
